what_it_is.prose: The Boeing C-17A Globemaster III is the Indian Air Force's heavy strategic airlift transport, operated by No. 81 Squadron 'Skylords' from Hindan Air Force Station near Delhi. India signed a US Foreign Military Sale for 10 C-17s in June 2011, valued at approximately $4.1 billion (about Rs 20,500 crore), to provide long-range strategic and tactical airlift and to progressively supplement the ageing Il-76 fleet. The first aircraft was delivered in January 2013 and formally accepted in June 2013; No. 81 Squadron was raised on 1 September 2013. Six aircraft were in hand by July 2014 and the initial ten were delivered by 2014. India subsequently obtained an eleventh aircraft — approved through a further US Foreign Military Sale in 2017 — which was delivered on 26 August 2019, taking the fleet to 11. The C-17 is powered by four Pratt & Whitney F117-PW-100 turbofans, can carry a payload on the order of 77 tonnes, and can operate from short, semi-prepared runways, making it central to Indian strategic mobility, high-altitude resupply along the northern borders, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. The Atlas treats the C-17 as a foreign-origin (US) platform in Indian service with no indigenous production content.

deployments_procurement.summary: India acquired the C-17 through US Foreign Military Sales: 10 aircraft under the ~$4.1 billion June 2011 deal, delivered 2013–2014, and an 11th approved via FMS in 2017 and delivered in August 2019. All 11 are operated by No. 81 Squadron 'Skylords' at Hindan, raised on 1 September 2013.

import_dependencies.summary: The C-17 is a wholly foreign-origin (US) platform acquired via Foreign Military Sales, with no Indian production content. The airframe, its four Pratt & Whitney F117 engines and all mission systems are imported, and the type is sustained through Boeing/US support arrangements. With the C-17 line closed since 2015, sustainment and spares depend entirely on the global support pool.

faq.question: How many C-17s does India operate and where are they based?
faq.answer: The Indian Air Force operates 11 Boeing C-17A Globemaster III aircraft with No. 81 Squadron 'Skylords' at Hindan Air Force Station near Delhi. The squadron was raised on 1 September 2013.

faq.question: How and when did India acquire the C-17?
faq.answer: India bought 10 C-17s under a US Foreign Military Sale worth about $4.1 billion (Rs 20,500 crore) signed in June 2011, with deliveries running from January 2013 to 2014. An 11th aircraft was approved through a further FMS in 2017 and delivered on 26 August 2019.

faq.question: Is the C-17 built or partly made in India?
faq.answer: No. The C-17 is a wholly US-origin Boeing platform acquired via Foreign Military Sales, with no Indian production content. Its four Pratt & Whitney F117 engines and all systems are imported, and — with the C-17 line closed since 2015 — the fleet is sustained through the global US/Boeing support pool.
